values.description: Under named-threat: the clusters name who conducts intrusions - threat actor groups, intrusion sets, and curated lists of entities operating or selling intrusion capability.
Under named-threat: the clusters name a bounded piece of intrusion activity - a campaign, an operation, a documented incident or case study against a specific target.
Under named-threat: the clusters name malicious software families - ransomware, RATs, stealers, bankers, botnets, wipers and the like.
Under named-threat: the clusters name software or services used in intrusions without being malware by design - dual-use and remote management tools, exploit kits, traffic distribution systems.

Under technique: ATT&CK-shaped techniques whose clusters carry a kill_chain element naming their tactic, so they can be rolled up by tactic. A property of the sub-category, not something to infer from kill_chain_order.
Under technique: techniques from a framework with its own tactic vocabulary - DISARM, AM!TT, SPARTA, fraud frameworks and the like - which do not belong on one tactic strip with ATT&CK.
Under technique: the clusters are the tactics themselves - the phases or goals of an intrusion - rather than the techniques used to reach them.
Under victim: the clusters name an activity sector or industry that was hit.
Under victim: the clusters name a place that was hit - a country or a region.
Under victim: the clusters describe what was targeted when it is neither a sector nor a place - a kind of target or of targeted information.
Under defensive: the clusters are courses of action, mitigations and countermeasures addressing specific adversary behaviour.
Under defensive: the clusters are controls or requirements from a security control catalogue or assurance framework, not tied to a specific technique.
Under detection: the clusters are detection rules ready to run against data - Sigma rules and the like.
Under detection: the clusters are analytics and detection strategies - how a behaviour would be caught, rather than a rule ready to run.
Under detection: the clusters name the data sources and data components a detection reads from.
Under targeting: the clusters name devices, equipment and infrastructure that can be exposed or attacked.
Under targeting: the clusters name platforms, such as operating systems.
Under targeting: the clusters name online services that can be exposed or abused.
Under context: the clusters name who produced the intelligence - the publisher of a report or a feed.
Under context: the clusters name organisations that appear alongside threat intelligence without being a threat themselves - vendors, agencies, institutions, listed entities.
Under context: the clusters name branded vulnerabilities - vulnerabilities known by a name rather than only an identifier.
Under context: the clusters are a reference list of sources used alongside threat intelligence - cited reports and publications, IP lists and the like.

description: The finer distinction inside a galaxy's category - actor vs malware within named-threat, for instance. Each value belongs to one category of galaxy-category, named at the start of its description; the reference category has none. Set on the galaxy definition, not on the cluster, and optional even when category is set.
author: MISP Project
